title: Competency gains drive a ratchet toward ever greater multiscale competency

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Competency gains drive a ratchet toward ever greater multiscale competency

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because each gain in developmental competency makes the structural genome harder for selection to evaluate, evolution increasingly optimizes the competency mechanisms themselves, a feedback ratchet for multiscale intelligence that appears in computational models and has run to different extents in planaria, salamanders and mammals.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › An evolutionary intelligence ratchet

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: This starts a feedback loop, because each gain in competency makes it even harder to judge the structural genome, which exacerbates the drive toward improving competencies—a ratchet for multiscale intelligence that can readily be seen in computational models of the process [240].

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology”, Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS (2023), doi:10.1007/s00018-023-04790-z; section “An evolutionary intelligence ratchet”. Scope: Evolution of metazoans; computational models of evolving competent cells

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-agential-17: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.48

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The feedback mechanism is testable in computational models with controlled architectures. Current data cannot establish that it operated to different extents across the named animal lineages or that modeled competency corresponds to biological intelligence.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In explicit evolutionary models, manipulate developmental error correction and measure whether selection shifts from structural parameters toward competency parameters over generations. Test for a monotonic feedback and compare evolved robustness among model lineages under matched mutation and fitness conditions.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Comparing planaria, salamanders, and mammals requires unavailable matched evolutionary histories.

Competency and intelligence require model-specific metrics.

The ratchet may be an artifact of genotype representation.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.48
analysis feasibility: 0.5
discriminating power: 0.58
operationalizability: 0.57
data adequacy: 0.3

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The computational ratchet is re-runnable from a public repository that already stores simulation outputs, so that part can be confirmed or refuted by a standard reanalysis. The claim also ranks real lineages, and nothing in the repository or in a comparable open table measures their competency. The model result is a proxy for the evolutionary statement, not the whole of it.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In the public competency model, track the fraction of fitness-improving changes that alter competency parameters versus structural genes as competency is allowed to evolve. An increasing share of competency edits, and weaker selection on the structural genome, would support the ratchet inside that model; continued improvement mainly in structural genes would refute it there.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The model uses a one-dimensional positional target, so its ratchet need not be the biological one.

Ordering planaria, salamanders, and mammals by degree of competency is not a variable in the saved runs.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.45

data existence: 0.72
operationalizability: 0.65
